en.name: Spaghetti squash, cut
en.summary: Once a spaghetti squash is cut the rules change completely: the hard rind that let a whole one sit in a cool room for two months is no longer protecting anything. Cut squash keeps 4–5 days refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below.
en.pantry: Cut spaghetti squash must not be left at room temperature. The exposed flesh is moist, low in acid and open to the air, which is a very different proposition from the sealed, rind-protected whole squash. There is no room-temperature figure here and none should be assumed. Refrigerate cut pieces immediately, and discard anything left out for more than two hours, or one hour above 32 °C (90 °F).
en.fridge: Wrap the cut faces tightly in cling film or put the pieces in a sealed container, and keep them at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, where they last 4–5 days. Scoop out the seeds and stringy centre before storing rather than after: that wet core is the first part to go, and removing it buys you the whole window. The cut faces will dry and discolour slightly whatever you do; trim a thin slice off before cooking if they look tired.
en.freezer: No freezer timeline is given for cut spaghetti squash, and freezing it raw is not the right approach — raw cut squash thaws watery and limp. Roast it first, pull the flesh into strands with a fork, cool it, drain it well and freeze the strands in portions at −18 °C (0 °F), where food stays safe indefinitely. No quality window has been published for the strands, so we do not quote one.
en.thawing: Reheat frozen cooked strands from frozen in a pan with the sauce, draining off the water they release. Do not thaw raw cut squash and expect to roast it well; it will steam rather than caramelise.
spoilage: Slimy or wet cut faces rather than merely dried
Mould on a cut surface or in the seed cavity
Flesh gone brown, grey or translucent
A sour or fermented smell when the wrapping comes off
tips: Scoop the seeds and stringy core out before storing, not before cooking.
Wrap the cut faces tightly; air is what dries and discolours them.
Trim a thin slice off a tired-looking cut face before roasting.
Roast cut-side down so the flesh steams in its own moisture and the strands separate cleanly.

faq.q: How long does cut spaghetti squash last?
faq.a: 4–5 days refrigerated at 4 °C (40 °F) or below, with the cut faces wrapped tightly and the seeds already scooped out.

faq.q: Can cut spaghetti squash be left out?
faq.a: No. The rind is what let a whole squash sit in a cool room; a cut one is a moist, low-acid food and belongs in the fridge within two hours.

faq.q: Can you freeze cut spaghetti squash?
faq.a: Not usefully raw, and no timeline is published. Roast it, fork the flesh into strands, drain and freeze the strands in portions at −18 °C (0 °F).

faq.q: Why should you remove the seeds before storing?
faq.a: The stringy seed cavity holds the most moisture and deteriorates first. Scooping it out before the squash goes in the fridge gives the rest of the flesh its full few days.

zh.name: 金絲瓜（切開）
zh.summary: 金絲瓜一旦切開，規則就完全不同了：讓整顆瓜能在涼爽室內放兩個月的那層硬皮，已經不再保護任何東西。切開的金絲瓜冷藏於 4°C 以下可放 4～5 天。
zh.pantry: 切開的金絲瓜絕對不能放室溫。裸露的瓜肉濕潤、低酸度又完全暴露在空氣中，和有硬皮包覆、密閉完整的整顆瓜是兩回事。這裡不提供常溫保存天數，也請不要自行推估。切開後請立刻冷藏；放在室溫超過兩小時（氣溫超過 32°C 時一小時）的請丟棄。
zh.fridge: 請把切面用保鮮膜緊貼包好，或整塊裝進密封容器，冷藏於 4°C 以下，可放 4～5 天。請在「保存前」就把籽和中間的絲狀囊挖掉，而不是等到要煮才挖：那團濕濕的中心是最先壞的部分，先清掉才能把整段保存期用滿。不論怎麼做，切面都會稍微乾掉變色；下鍋前看起來乾黃的話，薄薄削掉一層即可。
zh.freezer: 這裡不提供切開金絲瓜的冷凍保存期限，而且生的直接冷凍也不是正確做法——生切瓜解凍後會軟爛出水。請先烤熟，用叉子把果肉刮成絲，放涼、徹底瀝乾後分裝冷凍於 −18°C，在該溫度下安全上可無限期保存。瓜絲沒有公布的品質期限，所以我們不引用數字。
zh.thawing: 冷凍熟瓜絲請不解凍，直接連同醬汁下鍋加熱，並瀝掉釋出的水分。不要解凍生的切塊還指望烤得好，它只會一直冒水而烤不出焦香。
spoilage: 切面變得黏滑濕答答，而不只是乾掉
瓜肉轉褐、發灰或變得半透明
拆開包裝聞到酸味或發酵味
tips: 保存前就把籽和絲狀囊挖掉，不要留到要煮才處理。
切面包緊；空氣正是讓它乾掉變色的原因。
切面看起來乾黃的話，下鍋前薄削一層。
切面朝下烤，讓瓜肉在自身水氣中悶熟，瓜絲才會乾淨分離。

faq.q: 切開的金絲瓜可以放多久？
faq.a: 4°C 以下冷藏、切面包緊、籽先挖掉，可放 4～5 天。

faq.q: 切開的金絲瓜可以放室溫嗎？
faq.a: 不行。整顆能放涼爽室內靠的是那層硬皮；切開後它就是濕潤的低酸度食品，兩小時內要進冰箱。

faq.q: 切開的金絲瓜可以冷凍嗎？
faq.a: 生的直接冷凍沒什麼用，也沒有公布的期限。請先烤熟、刮成絲、瀝乾後分裝冷凍於 −18°C。

faq.q: 為什麼保存前要先把籽挖掉？
faq.a: 中間的絲狀籽囊含水最多、也最先劣化。放進冰箱前先清掉，其餘的瓜肉才能完整撐過那幾天。
